data.name: Aeneas
data.gender_notes: Aeneas is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Aeneas is a Latin name derived from the word aeneus, which means 'bronze' or 'honor'. In Roman mythology, Aeneas was a Trojan hero who led his people to Italy and founded the Roman race. He is known for his honor, courage, and mercy. The name Aeneas carries the meaning “Honor and Mercy” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Aeneas usually hope their child will grow to embody honor and mercy and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbol of perseverance and strength in the face of adversity.
data.etymology: Aeneas belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Honor and Mercy.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Aeneas total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

in_hebrew.name: אייניאס
in_hebrew.long_meaning: אייניאס הוא שם שמקורו ביוונית, אך הוא מופיע גם בברית הישנה כבן של אבינעזר, אחד מראשי העם היהודי. המשמעות העברית של השם אייניאס היא איש חזק ויציב, תומך נאמן, והוא משויך לאנשים חזקים ובעלי עמוד שדרה.

in_greek.name: Αἰνείας
in_greek.long_meaning: Αἰνείας είναι όνομα που προέρχεται από την ελληνική λέξη 'αἰνείας', που σημαίνει 'αιώνιος', 'αέναος'. Ο Αἰνείας ήταν ένας από τους ήρωες της Τροίας, και το όνομά του συνδέεται με την αέναη και αιώνια μνήμη.

in_latin.name: Aeneas
in_latin.long_meaning: Aeneas, derived from Greek 'Αἰνείας', signifies a strong and steadfast individual, one who is worthy of praise. In the context of early Christian church, the name Aeneas represents endurance and loyalty, reflecting the virtues esteemed by the early Christian community.

in_english.name: Aeneas
in_english.long_meaning: The name Aeneas originates from the Greek 'Αἰνείας', meaning 'praised' or 'strong'. In Christian tradition, Aeneas symbolizes strength, endurance, and loyalty. The biblical reference to Aeneas is found in Acts 9:33-35, where he is a disciple of Jesus Christ, healed by Peter. The name Aeneas signifies a person of strong character, faith, and perseverance.

data.cultural_impact: Aeneas is a classic and historically significant name in Western culture due to his role in Roman mythology. His name is often associated with strength, leadership, and resilience, as he led his people from the ruins of Troy to a new homeland.
data.spiritual_significance: In the spiritual context, the name Aeneas is a reminder of the importance of staying true to one's values and principles in the face of adversity. It is also a symbol of the journey of life, as Aeneas' journey represents the transformative power of faith, courage, and perseverance in overcoming obstacles and creating a new future. Additionally, the name Aeneas can be seen as a reflection of the spiritual journey toward enlightenment, as it signifies the desire to leave behind the old ways and embrace a new path.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Aeneas is a name of perseverance and divine guidance. Derived from the Latin word 'Aeneas', meaning 'unyielding' or 'inexhaustible', it symbolizes one's unwavering spirit and courage in the face of adversity. This name also holds a spiritual significance as it was the name of the legendary Trojan hero who, under the guidance of the goddess Venus, founded the Roman people.

biblical_reference.note: Aeneas was a disciple of Jesus Christ, healed by Peter.

historical_references.reference: Aeneas was a Trojan prince, traditionally considered a son of the god Aphrodite or Venus, who survived the Trojan War and, in the Aeneid, founded the Roman race.
historical_references.time_period: 12th or 13th century BC (Trojan War) to 1st century AD (Roman Empire)

historical_references.reference: Aeneas is also known from Virgil's epic poem the Aeneid, which describes his wanderings after the fall of Troy and his eventual arrival in Italy, where he becomes the ancestor of the Romans.

modern_usage.modern_context: Aeneas is a character from classical literature and mythology, best known for his role in Virgil's Aeneid. In modern contexts, Aeneas is frequently referenced in literature, mythology studies, and various artistic works. He is also a popular character in tabletop role-playing games and video games. For instance, in the tabletop RPG Dungeons & Dragons, Aeneas can be used as a historical NPC (non-player character) for campaigns based on ancient Rome. In video games, Aeneas has been featured in titles like Assassin's Creed: Origins and Total War: Rome II, where he is portrayed as a significant historical figure.

name_in_real_life.story: A devoted Christian named Grace Aeneas in Rome, Italy credits much of their spiritual journey to their name Aeneas, which means "Honor and Mercy". They believe their name has been a blessing and reminder of God's presence in their life.
